scenario: Discussing a news story with a colleague
frequency_note: words ranked ~700–1500 by frequency of Korean

vocabulary.note: Loanword from English 'news'. Used in general news contexts.
Refers to a written article in a newspaper or news site.
Used to emphasize the truth of something.
Used in discussion contexts to refer to a topic or difficulty.
Regular verb. Used to express opinions.
Commonly used in forms like '알고 있어요' (I already know).
Descriptive adjective. Can use '많은' to modify nouns.
Predicative adjective. Frequently used in discussions.
Used with negations or incomplete states.
Adversative connector. Used at the beginning of a sentence or between clauses.
Often appears as '~에 대해서' (about something).

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: 오늘 뉴스에서 본 기사에 대해서 어떻게 생각해요?
dialogue.translation: What do you think about the article I saw in the news today?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: 그 기사는 아직 다 읽지 못했어요. 그런데 사실인 것 같아요.
dialogue.translation: I haven't been able to read the whole article yet. But it seems to be true.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: 저도 그렇게 생각해요. 그런데 문제가 더 많은 것 같아요.
dialogue.translation: I think so too. But it seems there are more problems.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: 맞아요. 그 문제에 대해서는 정부가 뭐라고 했어요?
dialogue.translation: Right. What did the government say about that problem?

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: 아직 발표가 없어요. 그런데 전문가들은 중요하다고 말해요.
dialogue.translation: There's no announcement yet. But experts say it's important.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: 저도 그게 중요하다고 생각해요. 그런데 우리가 할 수 있는 일이 없네요.
dialogue.translation: I also think that's important. But there's nothing we can do.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: 그래도 우리가 이 기사에 대해서 알게 되면 도움이 될 거예요.
dialogue.translation: Still, if we get to know about this article, it will be helpful.

key_phrases.translation: I haven't been able to ~ yet

scenario: Negotiating a minor disagreement
frequency_note: words ranked ~700–1500 by frequency of Korean

vocabulary.note: Used in contexts of discussion or exchange of ideas.
Conjugates as 다르다 → 달라요 (polite form).
Regular verb in -하다.
Used to refer to a part of something abstract or concrete.
동의 + 하다. Used with 에게 or 와/과.
Noun used with 하다 to mean 'to propose'.
Used to accept an idea, proposal, or condition.
Can also be a noun (대신에).
Adverb of quantity. Used with verbs and adjectives.

vocabulary.translation: to be okay, to be acceptable
vocabulary.note: Polite form: 괜찮아요.
Contraction of 그렇게 하면. Used for logical transitions.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: 내 의견은 네 의견과 조금 달라요.
dialogue.translation: My opinion is a little different from yours.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: 이해해요. 하지만 그 부분은 제가 동의하기 어려워요.
dialogue.translation: I understand. But I find it hard to agree on that part.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: 제 제안을 받아들일 수 없어요?
dialogue.translation: Can't you accept my proposal?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: 아니요, 그건 아니에요. 대신 조금 바꾸면 괜찮을 것 같아요.
dialogue.translation: No, it's not that. Instead, if you change it a little, I think it will be fine.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: 그럼, 어떤 부분을 바꾸고 싶어요?
dialogue.translation: Then, which part do you want to change?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: 그 부분을 조금 더 쉽게 하면 제가 받아들일 수 있어요.
dialogue.translation: If you make that part a little easier, I can accept it.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: 좋아요. 그럼 그렇게 하기로 해요. 의견이 다르지만 괜찮은 해결책이네요.
dialogue.translation: Okay. Then let's do it that way. Even though opinions differ, it's a good solution.

scenario: Giving feedback on someone's work
frequency_note: words ranked ~700–1500 by frequency of Korean

vocabulary.note: Refers to the content of a text, speech, etc.
Adverb that emphasizes certainty or clarity.
Loanword from English, common in work and educational contexts.
Used to describe complete information or explanations.
Transitive verb; can also mean 'to repair' or 'to cure'.
Used as a noun or adjective: 마지막 부분 = the last part.
Relational adjective, used with 이다: 논리적이다 = to be logical.
Indicates that something is easy to understand or perceive.
Refers to documents, statistics, etc., for a work.
Transitive verb: 설명하다 + object.
Relational adjective: 효과적이다 = to be effective.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: 보고서 잘 봤어요. 내용이 확실히 좋아졌네요.
dialogue.translation: I read your report well. The content has clearly improved.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: 감사합니다. 피드백 주신 덕분에 많이 고쳤어요.
dialogue.translation: Thank you. Thanks to your feedback, I corrected a lot.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: 그런데 마지막 부분이 조금 아쉬워요. 논리적 연결이 분명하지 않아요.
dialogue.translation: But the last part is a bit disappointing. The logical connection is not clear.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: 네, 그 부분은 자료를 더 찾아서 설명하려고요.
dialogue.translation: Yes, for that part I plan to find more materials and explain it.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: 좋아요. 자료를 추가하면 훨씬 효과적일 거예요.
dialogue.translation: Good. If you add materials, it will be much more effective.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: 알겠어요. 그럼 다시 고쳐서 보여드릴게요.
dialogue.translation: Okay. Then I'll fix it again and show you.

key_phrases.translation: The logical connection is not clear
To find more materials and explain

scenario: Explaining a problem to customer service
frequency_note: words ranked ~700–1500 by frequency of Korean

vocabulary.note: Used for receiving objects, calls, emails, etc.
Common in customer service contexts.
In online shopping.
Noun form of 확인하다.

vocabulary.translation: to ask a favor, to request
vocabulary.note: Polite way to ask for something.
Used for data, information, etc.
Used for services, facilities, etc.
Used for situations or problems.
Common in problems with products or services.
Used to indicate the current moment.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: 안녕하세요. 주문한 물건을 아직 받지 못했습니다. 확인해 주시겠어요?
dialogue.translation: Hello. I haven't received the item I ordered yet. Could you check it?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: 죄송합니다. 주문 번호와 배송 주소를 확인해 주시겠어요?
dialogue.translation: We're sorry. Could you verify your order number and delivery address?

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: 네, 주문 번호는 12345이고 배송 주소는 그대로입니다. 그런데 배송 상태가 지금도 '준비 중'으로 나와요.
dialogue.translation: Yes, the order number is 12345 and the delivery address is the same. But the shipping status still shows 'preparing'.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: 확인해 보겠습니다. 잠시만요. 정확한 정보를 확인하기 위해 시간이 조금 걸릴 수 있습니다.
dialogue.translation: Let me check. Just a moment. It may take a little time to confirm the exact information.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: 알겠습니다. 그런데 이 문제를 해결하는 게 어렵지 않을까요?
dialogue.translation: I see. But won't it be difficult to resolve this problem?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: 걱정하지 마세요. 저희가 빠르게 해결하도록 노력하겠습니다. 이용해 주셔서 감사합니다.
dialogue.translation: Don't worry. We'll do our best to resolve it quickly. Thank you for using our service.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: 네, 부탁드립니다. 좋은 결과 기대할게요.
dialogue.translation: Yes, please. I look forward to a good outcome.

key_phrases.translation: We will do our best to resolve it.

scenario: Talking about ambitions and career goals
frequency_note: words ranked ~700–1500 by frequency of Korean

vocabulary.note: Used to refer to the coming time or future prospects.
Common in contexts of goals and projects.
Used for personal goals or aspirations.
Frequent with 꿈: 꿈을 이루다 = to make a dream come true.
Used in contexts of professional achievements.
Often with 하다: 노력하다 = to make an effort.
Adjectival verb that governs an object with 이/가.
With 하다: 준비하다 = to prepare (oneself).
In expressions like 마음이 정하다 = to have decided.
Used with goals or plans.
Common in contexts of perseverance.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: 나는 미래에 대한 계획을 세우고 있어. 꿈을 이루기 위해 준비를 시작했어.
dialogue.translation: I am making plans for the future. I have started preparing to make my dream come true.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: 좋은 생각이야! 나는 아직 확실히 정하지 못했지만, 성공하려면 많은 노력이 필요하다고 생각해.
dialogue.translation: Good idea! I haven't decided for sure yet, but I think you need a lot of effort to succeed.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: 맞아. 나는 마음이 정해졌어. 어떤 어려움이 있어도 포기하지 않을 거야.
dialogue.translation: Right. My mind is made up. I won't give up no matter what difficulties arise.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: 그런 결심이 중요하지. 나도 구체적인 계획을 세워야겠다. 어떤 준비를 하고 있어?
dialogue.translation: That kind of determination is important. I should also make a concrete plan. What preparation are you doing?

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: 매일 공부하고, 관련 경험을 쌓고 있어. 그리고 멘토에게 조언도 받아.
dialogue.translation: I study every day and gain related experience. I also get advice from a mentor.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: 좋은 방법이네. 나는 아직 망설이고 있는데, 네 이야기를 들으니 나도 꿈을 향해 나아가고 싶어.
dialogue.translation: That's a good method. I'm still hesitating, but hearing your story makes me want to move toward my dream too.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: 함께 힘내자. 우리의 미래를 위해 지금부터 차근차근 준비하자!
dialogue.translation: Let's cheer up together. Let's prepare step by step from now on for our future!

key_phrases.translation: to make a dream come true

scenario: Discussing health habits and lifestyle
frequency_note: words ranked ~700–1500 by frequency of Korean

vocabulary.note: Common noun used to refer to health in general.
Used for both positive and negative habits.
Refers to physical exercise, not specific sports.

vocabulary.translation: meal, meal (as the act of eating)
vocabulary.note: Refers to a meal as an action or a main meal (breakfast, lunch, dinner).
Adverb used to indicate regularity or consistency in an action.
Transitive verb: used with a direct object (e.g., reduce sugar).
Noun describing physical or mental tiredness.
Loanword from English 'stress', very common in Korean.

vocabulary.translation: to be adequate, to be moderate
vocabulary.note: Used to indicate that something is appropriate in quantity or intensity.
Adjective describing something that occurs regularly, such as routines.
Conjunction that adds additional information, similar to 'furthermore' in English.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: 요즘 건강을 위해서 뭘 하고 있어요?
dialogue.translation: What are you doing these days for your health?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: 아침마다 꾸준히 운동을 해요. 그리고 식사도 규칙적으로 하려고 노력해요.
dialogue.translation: I exercise consistently every morning. And I also try to have regular meals.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: 좋은 습관이네요. 저는 요즘 피로가 많아서 스트레스를 줄이려고 해요.
dialogue.translation: That's a good habit. Lately I've been very tired, so I'm trying to reduce stress.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: 스트레스를 줄이려면 적당한 운동이 도움이 돼요. 게다가 충분한 수면도 중요해요.
dialogue.translation: To reduce stress, moderate exercise helps. Furthermore, getting enough sleep is also important.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: 맞아요. 저도 이제부터 운동을 꾸준히 해야겠어요.
dialogue.translation: That's right. From now on, I should also exercise consistently.

key_phrases.translation: for health, for the sake of health

scenario: Describing a recent trip in detail
frequency_note: words ranked ~700–1500 by frequency of Korean

vocabulary.note: common noun for trip
basic movement verb
in this context, 'report' of the experience
photograph
intensifier
conjunction to add information
descriptive adjective
used with '에' to indicate 'for the first time'
temporal expression
superlative
to arrive at a destination

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: 저번 주말에 부산에 처음 갔어.
dialogue.translation: Last weekend I went to Busan for the first time.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: 정말? 여행이 어땠어?
dialogue.translation: Really? How was the trip?

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: 정말 재미있었어. 그리고 바다가 가장 좋았어.
dialogue.translation: It was really fun. And the best part was the sea.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: 사진 많이 찍었어? 보고 싶어.
dialogue.translation: Did you take many photos? I want to see them.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: 응, 그런데 배터리가 없어서 마지막에 사진을 많이 못 찍었어.
dialogue.translation: Yes, but the battery ran out, so I couldn't take many photos at the end.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: 아쉽다. 다음에 또 가면 꼭 보여줘.
dialogue.translation: That's a shame. If you go again, be sure to show me.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: 그래, 다음에는 도착하자마자 배터리 충전할 거야.
dialogue.translation: Yeah, next time I'll charge the battery as soon as I arrive.

scenario: Talking about environmental issues
frequency_note: words ranked ~700–1500 by frequency of Korean

vocabulary.note: Frequently used in ecological contexts and also for 'surroundings'.
Combines with '공기' (air), '물' (water), etc.
Used for problems, situations, etc.
Very frequent word; in context it can be an environmental problem.
Used to talk about the planet in general.
Common in discussions about climate change.
In this context, it refers to the temperature rising. Also used for prices, levels, etc.
Used with resources, quantity, etc. Do not confuse with '줄이다' (transitive) which they already know.
Regular verb in -하다.
Noun used with '있다/없다'. Similar to 'to need'.
Indicates company or joint action.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: 요즘 환경 문제가 정말 심각하네요.
dialogue.translation: These days, environmental problems are really serious.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: 맞아요. 특히 지구의 온도가 계속 올라가고 있어요.
dialogue.translation: That's right. Especially the Earth's temperature keeps rising.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: 그래서 공기 오염도 점점 심해지고, 물도 줄고 있어요.
dialogue.translation: So air pollution is getting worse and water is decreasing too.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: 우리가 환경을 보호하기 위해서 꼭 필요한 일이 뭘까요?
dialogue.translation: What is the essential thing we need to do to protect the environment?

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: 우선 쓰레기를 줄이고, 에너지를 아끼는 게 중요해요.
dialogue.translation: First, it's important to reduce waste and save energy.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: 맞아요. 우리 모두 함께 노력해야 해요.
dialogue.translation: That's right. We all need to work together.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: 그럼 우리 작은 것부터 시작해요.
dialogue.translation: Then let's start with the small things.

scenario: Discussing a decision you had to make
frequency_note: words ranked ~700–1500 by frequency of Korean

vocabulary.note: Regular verb, used with a direct object or clause.
Frequently used with 하다: 고민하다 = to worry, to think a lot.
Used with 하다: 선택하다 = to choose.
Used to refer to concrete or abstract results.
Used with 으로: 기준으로 = as a criterion.
Used with 와/과: A와 B를 비교하다.
Descriptive adjective, used with 이/가.
Used to affirm something obvious.
Indicates a result after a process.
Used to indicate substitution or compensation.
Used after a noun or nominalized verb.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: 요즘 새로운 직장을 선택할지 고민이 많아.
dialogue.translation: Lately I have a lot of worries about whether to choose a new job.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: 어떤 기준으로 비교하고 있어?
dialogue.translation: By what criteria are you comparing?

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: 급여도 중요하지만, 결과적으로 내가 좋아하는 일을 하는 게 더 중요하다고 생각해.
dialogue.translation: Salary is important too, but I think that in the end, doing what I like is more important.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: 물론이지. 그런데 결정하기 전에 두 회사를 더 자세히 비교해 봐.
dialogue.translation: Of course. But before deciding, compare the two companies in more detail.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: 그래서 결국 내가 가장 좋아하는 분야의 회사를 선택했어. 대신에 연봉은 조금 낮아졌지만.
dialogue.translation: So in the end I chose the company in the field I like most. In exchange, the salary went down a bit.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: 좋은 결정이야. 그 선택 때문에 오히려 더 만족스러울 거야.
dialogue.translation: Good decision. Because of that choice, you'll actually be more satisfied.

key_phrases.translation: I have many worries / I'm very indecisive
to compare according to the criteria of...

scenario: Explaining why you changed your mind
frequency_note: words ranked ~700–1500 by frequency of Korean

vocabulary.note: Commonly used to express changing one's mind: '생각이 바뀌다' (to change one's mind).
Intransitive verb, opposite of 바꾸다 (to change something).
Used in both formal and informal contexts.
Transitive verb, with direct object: '~을/를 설명하다'.
Also used as an adverb for emphasis: '사실은...' (actually...).
In context: '알게 되다' (to come to know) is common for explaining a change of mind.

vocabulary.translation: to be different, to be distinct
vocabulary.note: Conjugates: '달라요' (polite), '다르다' (base form).
Used with negative forms: '전혀 안 ~'.
Indicates contrast with what is expected.
Common connector at the start of a sentence to contrast.
In context: '약속을 바꾸다' (to change a plan).

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: 야, 너 내일 같이 영화 보기로 한 거 기억하지? 그런데 내 생각이 좀 바뀌었어.
dialogue.translation: Hey, you remember we agreed to watch a movie together tomorrow, right? But I've changed my mind a bit.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: 응? 갑자기 왜? 무슨 이유가 있어?
dialogue.translation: Huh? Why suddenly? Is there a reason?

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: 사실은 어제 친구한테 그 영화에 대해 들었어. 그 영화가 내가 생각했던 것과 전혀 달라서 실망할 것 같아.
dialogue.translation: Actually, yesterday I heard about that movie from a friend. It's completely different from what I thought, so I think I'd be disappointed.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: 그래? 그런데 그 친구 말만 믿고 약속을 바꾸는 게 맞아?
dialogue.translation: Really? But is it right to change the plan just based on what that friend said?

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: 오히려 그 친구 말을 듣고 나서 더 확신이 생겼어. 그 영화 대신 다른 걸 보는 게 좋겠어.
dialogue.translation: On the contrary, after listening to that friend, I became more convinced. It'd be better to watch something else instead of that movie.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: 음, 그럼 왜 그런지 좀 더 설명해 봐. 나는 아직 잘 모르겠어.
dialogue.translation: Hmm, then explain a bit more why. I still don't understand well.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: 알겠어. 내가 그 영화에 대한 기대가 너무 컸던 것 같아. 그리고 줄거리를 알고 보니 내 취향이 아니더라고. 그래서 보기 전에 마음을 바꾼 거야.
dialogue.translation: Okay. I think my expectations for that movie were too high. And after learning the plot, I saw it's not my taste. So I changed my mind before watching it.

scenario: Talking about cultural differences
frequency_note: words ranked ~700–1500 by frequency of Korean

vocabulary.note: Used to refer to culture in general or a specific culture.
Commonly used to talk about differences between things or people.
Indicates reciprocity.
Regular -하다 verb.
Refers to a person's attitude or disposition.
Irregular adjective: 다르- + -ㄴ → 다른.
Can refer to personal or abstract relationships.
Used both for lived experience and acquired knowledge.
Ends in -하다, but is an adjective.

vocabulary.translation: through, by means of, to communicate
vocabulary.note: Often used as '~을 통해' (through).
Refers to norms of courtesy.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: 한국과 스페인의 문화 차이에 대해 어떻게 생각해?
dialogue.translation: What do you think about the cultural differences between Korea and Spain?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: 음, 제일 큰 차이는 서로 대화하는 태도인 것 같아. 한국에서는 나이 많은 사람에게 예절을 지키는 게 중요해.
dialogue.translation: Hmm, I think the biggest difference is the attitude in how we talk to each other. In Korea, it's important to show respect to elders.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: 그래? 나는 스페인에서는 좀 더 자유롭게 말하는 편이야. 그런데 문화가 다르다고 해서 관계가 나쁜 건 아니지?
dialogue.translation: Really? In Spain, I tend to speak more freely. But just because the culture is different doesn't mean the relationship is bad, right?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: 맞아. 다양한 경험을 통해 서로를 이해하는 게 중요해.
dialogue.translation: Right. It's important to understand each other through diverse experiences.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: 맞아. 나도 한국에 있을 때 그런 경험이 있었어. 처음에는 어색했지만, 시간이 지나면서 이해하게 됐어.
dialogue.translation: Right. I had that experience too when I was in Korea. At first it was awkward, but over time I came to understand.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: 그래서 나는 다른 문화를 배우는 게 좋아. 서로 다른 점을 알면 더 좋은 관계를 만들 수 있잖아.
dialogue.translation: That's why I like learning about other cultures. If we know our differences, we can build better relationships.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: 맞아. 앞으로도 다양한 문화를 경험하면서 서로 이해하는 태도를 가지려고 해.
dialogue.translation: Right. From now on, I want to have an attitude of understanding each other while experiencing diverse cultures.

dialogue.speaker: A

dialogue.speaker: B

dialogue.speaker: A
